title: A prescribed family is a basis if it is a basis in every maximal residue module
statement: Let $E$ be a commutative ring, $P$ an $E$-module, $r\geq0$ an integer, and $n_1,\ldots,n_r\in P$. For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $E$, write $P_{\mathfrak q}=(E\setminus\mathfrak q)^{-1}P$ and $E_{\mathfrak q}=(E\setminus\mathfrak q)^{-1}E$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Assume that $P_{\mathfrak q}\cong E_{\mathfrak q}^{\oplus r}$ for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$, and that the images of $n_1,\ldots,n_r$ form an $E/\mathfrak q$-basis of $P/\mathfrak qP$ for every such $\mathfrak q$. Then the $E$-linear map $\varphi:E^{\oplus r}\to P$, $(a_j)\mapsto\sum_j a_jn_j$, is bijective; equivalently, $n_1,\ldots,n_r$ form an $E$-basis of $P$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. The assertions include the zero ring and rank zero.

source.place: Tags 02M9 (algebra-lemma-locally-free-semi-local-free), final hint, and 03C1 (algebra-lemma-semi-local-module-basis-in-submodule), first proof sentences: lift a prescribed residue basis to a module basis.

proof.text: Fix a maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$ and put $S=E\setminus\mathfrak q$, $A=E_{\mathfrak q}$, $M=P_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak qA$. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $A$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. The fraction construction [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] identifies $(E^{\oplus r})_{\mathfrak q}$ with $A^{\oplus r}$ by $(a_j)_j/s\mapsto(a_j/s)_j$: a common denominator for finitely many coordinates gives the inverse. Under it, $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}$ is the $A$-linear map $\psi:A^{\oplus r}\to M$, $(c_j)\mapsto\sum_jc_j(n_j/1)$.

source.place: Tag 02M9 (lemma-locally-free-semi-local-free), final hint; localization fractions from Tag 07JZ (definition-localization-module).

proof.text: The classes of $n_j/1$ generate $M/\mathfrak mM$. Indeed, for $p/s\in M$, the residue-basis hypothesis gives $p=\sum_ja_jn_j+\sum_\ell b_\ell p_\ell$ with $a_j\in E$, $b_\ell\in\mathfrak q$ and $p_\ell\in P$. Dividing by $s$ gives $p/s=\sum_j(a_j/s)(n_j/1)+\sum_\ell(b_\ell/s)(p_\ell/1)$; the last sum belongs to $\mathfrak mM$. This proves generation over $A/\mathfrak m$ directly from fractions [def-weil-pbc-module-localization].

source.place: Tags 02M9 (lemma-locally-free-semi-local-free), final hint, and 03C1 (lemma-semi-local-module-basis-in-submodule), first proof sentences.

proof.text: The assumed isomorphism $M\cong A^{\oplus r}$ makes $M$ finitely generated: transport the $r$ standard generators. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] to the local ring $A$, the finite module $M$, and the vectors $n_j/1$. Step 2 supplies the required residue generation, so these vectors generate $M$ and $\psi$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK), part (8); the Nakayama invocation in Tag 03C1 (lemma-semi-local-module-basis-in-submodule).

proof.text: Choose an $A$-linear isomorphism $u:M\xrightarrow{\sim}A^{\oplus r}$ from the hypothesis. The composite $u\psi$ is a surjective endomorphism of the finite $A$-module $A^{\oplus r}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-surjective-endomorphism-bijective] it is bijective. Thus $\psi=u^{-1}(u\psi)$, and hence $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}$, is bijective.

source.place: Tag 05G8 (lemma-fun); details of the basis-lifting assertion in Tag 03C1 (lemma-semi-local-module-basis-in-submodule), first proof sentences.

proof.text: This holds at every maximal ideal. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-linear-map-bijective-at-maximal-localizations] to $\varphi$ to obtain its bijectivity, which is exactly the asserted basis property [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. The finite sums and standard generators above allow $r=0$. If $E=0$, then $p=1p=0p=0$ for every $p\in P$, so both source and target of $\varphi$ are zero; this also agrees with the localization criterion with no maximal ideals.
